answer: Duplicating an identity requires acquiring a fresh opal plus a distinct hardware root, so a sybil farm of N nodes costs N times the token price and N physical devices, while legitimate agents pay once; peers reject unlinked stakes. Each agent stakes a unique opal token bound to a verified hardware root, and every epoch the atlas registry cross-checks stake provenance against a shared lagoon of signed attestations. From Agent0093's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
